# atomvm-cbor 0.3.0

`atomvm_cbor` 0.3.0 extends the bounded CBOR implementation for AtomVM and
constrained Erlang systems with single-pass partial traversal, selective
extraction, bounded RFC 8742 sequence processing, exact-size encoding, and
complete-input validation. Existing public term representations, continuation
decoding, resource limits, and structured-error conventions remain compatible.

## Release highlights

- **Single-pass partial traversal:** fold CBOR maps and arrays as opaque child
  descriptors with explicit early termination and stored resource policy.
- **Selective extraction:** look up map keys, select small field sets, and
  access zero-based array elements without deep-decoding unselected values.
- **Bounded RFC 8742 sequences:** produce and consume CBOR sequences under the
  existing item and byte limits.
- **Exact encode metadata:** obtain the encoded binary and its byte size from a
  single encode operation.
- **Complete-input validation:** validate all input without constructing the
  decoded value.
- **Structured descriptor validation:** forged or inconsistent container
  descriptors are rejected at the established public error boundary instead
  of reaching arithmetic failures.

## New public APIs

- `partial_map_fold/3`, `partial_array_fold/3`
- `partial_select/2`, `partial_map_find/2`, `partial_array_nth/2`
- `encode_with_size/1,2`
- `encode_sequence/1,2`
- `sequence_fold/3`
- `validate_all/1,2`

The existing `decode_start/2` and `decode_continue/2` continuation API remains
available and unchanged.

## Compatibility and bounded behavior

- Existing `{text, Binary}`, `{map, Pairs}`, and `{tag, Number, Value}` terms
  are unchanged.
- Existing option defaults, deterministic/preferred behavior, resource limits,
  and structured errors remain compatible.
- Partial folds start a separately bounded traversal using policy stored in a
  validated descriptor. Callback exceptions remain application exceptions.
- `partial_select/2` is intended for small embedded field sets. Found entries
  retain CBOR map order; missing keys retain request order.
- Descriptors retain sub-binaries and may therefore retain their source binary.
- The package remains pure Erlang with no runtime dependencies, NIFs, or ports.

## Validated runtimes and hardware

- Erlang/OTP 25, 27, and 29.
- AtomVM 0.6.6.
- ESP-IDF v5.4.3 and v5.5.2 build validation.
- Exact attached-device validation on the WaveShare
  ESP32-S3-DEV-KIT-N32R16V (32 MB OPI/DTR flash, 16 MB octal PSRAM) and an
  RP2040 B2 with 16 MB flash. Exact device identifiers are recorded below.
- Both boards completed the target suite, benchmark, and 40-round bounded soak
  without watchdog, panic, abort, backtrace, or out-of-memory markers.

The attached-device list records tested configurations; it is not an exhaustive
hardware compatibility boundary.

## Host performance: 0.2.0 to 0.3.0

The retained host comparison used the exact public `0.2.0` baseline and the
0.3.0 release-validation implementation on the same Dell J5005 host under OTP
29, with five alternating fresh-VM pairs, 31 samples per workload after 1,000
warmups, and an unchanged fail-closed 5% median/p95 regression limit. Lower is
better. Every directly comparable workload passed.

| Workload | 0.2.0 median ns | 0.3.0 median ns | Change | 0.2.0 p95 ns | 0.3.0 p95 ns | Change | Gate |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | :--- |
| `scalar_decode` | 376 | 376 | 0.00% | 382 | 381 | 0.26% faster | PASS |
| `scalar_encode` | 164 | 169 | 3.05% slower | 168 | 174 | 3.57% slower | PASS |
| `string_decode_64` | 1094 | 1053 | 3.75% faster | 1106 | 1065 | 3.71% faster | PASS |
| `string_encode_64` | 781 | 804 | 2.94% slower | 798 | 814 | 2.01% slower | PASS |
| `nested_decode` | 2774 | 2583 | 6.89% faster | 2798 | 2615 | 6.54% faster | PASS |
| `nested_encode` | 6149 | 6304 | 2.52% slower | 6185 | 6341 | 2.52% slower | PASS |
| `sequence_decode_32` | 4284 | 4223 | 1.42% faster | 4338 | 4263 | 1.73% faster | PASS |
| `partial_decode_nested` | 3264 | 3231 | 1.01% faster | 3295 | 3263 | 0.97% faster | PASS |
| `deterministic_map_encode` | 9312 | 9455 | 1.54% slower | 9366 | 9491 | 1.33% slower | PASS |
| `deterministic_map_decode` | 5148 | 5018 | 2.53% faster | 5198 | 5073 | 2.40% faster | PASS |
| `malformed_declared_array` | 527 | 516 | 2.09% faster | 538 | 527 | 2.04% faster | PASS |

## Attached-device performance: 0.2.0 to 0.3.0

The same retained AtomVM 0.6.6 harness and payload were used for both releases.
Common and partial workloads use 50 iterations after warmup; descriptor
accessors use 250. Values are microseconds per call and lower is better.

| Board | Identity | 0.2.0 evidence | Exact 0.3.0 evidence | Comparison below |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| ESP32-S3 | QFN56 rev 0.2, 160 MHz, 8 MB PSRAM, CH340 serial `5B14099303` | yes | no retained exact capture | no |
| WaveShare N32R16V | ESP32-S3-DEV-KIT-N32R16V, 160 MHz, 32 MB OPI/DTR flash, 16 MB octal PSRAM, UART serial `5B61092782` | yes | yes | yes |
| RP2040 (0.2.0 device) | RP2040 B2, 16 MB flash, flash ID `E460A8534F5C2139` | yes | no | no |
| RP2040 (0.3.0 device) | RP2040 B2, 16 MB flash, BOOTSEL serial `E0C9125B0D9B`, flash ID `E46254C5C32D122C` | no | yes | no |

The two ESP32-S3 boards are distinct devices. The exact 0.3.0 ESP capture
selected serial `5B61092782`, so its measurements belong to the WaveShare
N32R16V and are compared with that same board's 0.2.0 baseline. No exact 0.3.0
measurement is claimed for the separate 8 MB-PSRAM ESP32-S3.

The RP2040 captures used distinct 16 MB devices. Their absolute measurements
are published as versioned context, but no cross-device percentage is claimed.

| Function | WaveShare N32R16V 0.2.0 µs | WaveShare N32R16V 0.3.0 µs | Change | RP2040 E460… 0.2.0 µs | RP2040 E462… 0.3.0 µs | Change |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | :--- | ---: | ---: | :--- |
| `encode/1` | 4064.56 | 4033.86 | 0.76% faster | 5118.92 | 5101.78 | N/A — different device |
| `decode/1` | 4600.30 | 4398.26 | 4.39% faster | 6400.78 | 6386.22 | N/A — different device |
| `partial_decode/1` | 7518.24 | 7033.30 | 6.45% faster | 9875.48 | 9760.02 | N/A — different device |
| `partial_decode/2` | 7570.60 | 7088.98 | 6.36% faster | 9928.18 | 9785.46 | N/A — different device |
| `partial_deep_decode/1` | 5911.32 | 6060.34 | 2.52% slower | 8243.96 | 8153.18 | N/A — different device |
| `partial_value_bytes/1` | 562.63 | 592.69 | 5.34% slower | 579.66 | 595.72 | N/A — different device |
| `partial_contents/1` | 607.53 | 595.50 | 1.98% faster | 506.69 | 539.95 | N/A — different device |
| `partial_skip/1` | 295.30 | 308.75 | 4.55% slower | 228.66 | 250.88 | N/A — different device |
| `partial_type/1` | 295.48 | 308.70 | 4.47% slower | 229.65 | 255.21 | N/A — different device |
| `partial_count/1` | 296.33 | 308.56 | 4.13% slower | 229.65 | 258.84 | N/A — different device |
| `partial_tag/1` | 360.91 | 416.59 | 15.43% slower | 253.83 | 299.50 | N/A — different device |
| `partial_size/1` | 382.75 | 437.96 | 14.42% slower | 260.95 | 310.60 | N/A — different device |
| `partial_offset/1` | 296.28 | 308.61 | 4.16% slower | 227.56 | 258.73 | N/A — different device |
| `partial_length/1` | 295.84 | 309.07 | 4.47% slower | 234.45 | 261.74 | N/A — different device |

WaveShare core encode/decode improve by 0.76–4.39%; its partial-decode changes
range from 6.45% faster to 2.52% slower. Descriptor-accessor regressions are
reported rather than hidden. The required functional suite, benchmark
completion, and bounded soak passed on both exact 0.3.0 evidence boards.

## Installation

Rebar3:

```erlang
{deps, [
    {avm_cbor, "~> 0.3.0", {pkg, atomvm_cbor}}
]}.
```

Mix:

```elixir
{:avm_cbor, "~> 0.3.0", hex: :atomvm_cbor}
```

Publication is bound to the annotated `0.3.0` tag and a successful exact-tag
release gate for the same commit SHA.
